chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: The market for female singers after 'Loch Lomond'
summary: Milt Gabler's claim that her success opened a market for female singers like Billie Holiday; she says most singers had been band vocalists.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Oh yes, and I also came across in the book by Arnold Shaw on 52nd Street a quotation which is contributed to Milt Gabler who said that it was your success at the Onyx Club, which opened up the
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
market for female singers. That was what was responsible for Cafe Society Downtown for putting in Billy Holiday for the longest successful one that she did there.

Well, as you know up until the time I did Loch Lomand most of the singers on records was just band singers. And there would be an orchestra arrangement and maybe the singer would come in and do a chorus. But my recording of Loch Lomand was actually a singer's record. Now, this wasn't a first because you must remember that Ethel Waters and some of the other singers had their own, not their own labels, but they were the featured singers and they did their recordings with an accompaniment, so to speak. So this might have been maybe a revival of that sort of thing. But, the idea of a song going on as an act in a Club might have had something to do with that.
